messages:
Maya: Heads-up: after the release merge (release/v1.23 -> main) we're seeing 2x p99 on small-batch inference. Likely kernel selector change + KV cache interaction. Observed ~120ms -> ~240ms p99 on cpu-optimized instances.
Liam: Ugh. CI perf job flagged something yesterday? @deploy-bot did the release go out automatically?
deploy-bot: Release pipeline: deployment to canary completed (sha: a1b2c3d). No rollback triggered.
Sasha: Can you paste the perf numbers + a minimal repro? need to triage whether it's batch heuristics or kernel fallback.
Maya: Quick numbers from prod-samplestore: baseline (pre-merge) p50/p95/p99 = 18/72/120ms, current = 20/110/240ms. Throughput steady. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~8% for short-context flows.
Nathan: If KV hit-rate drops and kernel selector picks slower kernels for short sequences that explains it. We pushed a kernel chooser tweak in cf12345.
Oliver: Can we bisect to confirm commit? We should avoid full revert until we know which change.
Maya: I ran a quick local bisect: reverted cf12345 locally and p99 returned to ~125ms. Re-applied and regression returns. So cf12345 is the likely culprit.
Sasha: Nice. What's in cf12345? I recall it changed kernel ranking to prefer wider matmul kernels at <=64 seq len to improve throughput for long batched workloads.
Liam: That makes sense — for small-batch short-seq requests the new path has higher setup + cache miss behavior.
Maya: Repro repro steps (short):
```
# run perf harness for 32-token samples
./tools/perf-run --model r-infer-3b --batch 1 --seq 32 --warm 200 --iter 1000
``` 
Compare with/without cf12345.
Nathan: OK. Plan proposals:
- revert cf12345 on main asap (fast rollback)
- cherry-pick revert into release/v1.23 and run release CI perf job
- create follow-up PR to refactor kernel selector to consider KV cache hit probability before preferring wider kernels
Sasha: Agree. Also add canary gating: when reverting, we should push to canary and watch p99 for 1h before full rollout.
Maya: I opened revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1845 (revert commit cf12345)
Liam: I'll queue cherry-pick to release branch once PR is merged. Command I'll run:
```
git checkout release/v1.23
git cherry-pick -x <revert-commit-sha>
git push origin release/v1.23:release/v1.23-hotfix-kv
``` 
Sasha: FYI add label `perf-regression` and assign to eng-runtime on the backport PR.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline started for PR #1845. Perf jobs: perf/e2e-short, perf/ci-bench
Maya: Running perf harness on the PR build now. Will paste numbers when done.
(30m later)
Maya: Quick results from PR build: p50/p95/p99 = 19/75/130ms — back to near-baseline. KV hit-rate restored.
Nathan: Great. Merge and cherry-pick to release.
Liam: Cherry-pick PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1846 (backport to v1.23)
Oliver: QA: I'll run a controlled canary deploy on prod-canary and monitor the `inference.p99` dashboard for 1 hour.
Sasha: Also add a small synthetic load that exercises short sequences to the canary load generator.
deploy-bot: Release canary deploy queued (sha: revert-sha). Rollout plan: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics stable.
Maya: Canary 10% deployed. Initial p99 looks good.
Oliver: 1h check-in: p99 stable, no errors.
Sasha: Approved for full rollout from eng-runtime.
Liam: Merged cherry-pick into release branch and kicked patch release build.
deploy-bot: Patch build artifact published: s3://redwood-releases/v1.23.1/release.tar.gz
Maya: Postmortem notes: kernel selector change didn't account for KV cache miss probability; needs an input signal from KV estimator. Filing follow-up ticket: RTF-872.
Nathan: For next release let's add perf-signoff step for kernel selector PRs with perf sim on both small-batch and bulk-batch patterns.
Sasha: Agreed. Also add a CI regression alert that fails PRs if p99 increases > 20% for short-seq perf suite.
Maya: Thanks everyone. Good catch and quick turnaround. :tada:
Oliver: Can we close this thread when the release tag is cut and docs updated?
Maya: Will follow up with release tag + postmortem link once done.
